hunks.baseline: Blood that had shot high like a fountain was falling onto my head, soaking my scalp.
hunks.sol: Blood that had shot up like a fountain fell onto my head, soaking my scalp.

hunks.baseline: For someone already reduced to a headless corpse, it was a sensation they would never feel again.
hunks.sol: Someone who was already a headless corpse would never feel it again.

hunks.baseline: The body, losing its balance a moment later, crumpled onto the pool of blood.
hunks.sol: A moment later, the body lost its balance and collapsed into the pool of blood.

hunks.baseline: The Second Elder’s head had been severed from his body before he’d had a chance to react. With a bewildered expression, it looked up at his sworn brothers.
hunks.sol: The Second Elder’s head had come off before he could even react. With a bewildered expression, it looked up at his sworn brothers.

hunks.baseline: Or, more precisely, the only sworn brother still in this world.
hunks.sol: Or rather, at the only sworn brother still in this world.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang’s timely words announced the Third Elder’s end. I turned to look and saw a silver blade sticking out of the back of the man sprawled like a rotten log.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang’s words marked the Third Elder’s end. I turned and saw a silver blade jutting from the back of the man sprawled like a rotten log.

hunks.baseline: Sama Pyo was retrieving the dagger lodged between the Third Elder’s brows. When our eyes met, he shrugged.
hunks.sol: Sama Pyo pulled the dagger from between the dead Third Elder’s brows. When our eyes met, he shrugged.

hunks.baseline: I answered.
A question crept into Sama Pyo’s gaze. I exhaled a breath as hot as a ball of fire and continued.
hunks.sol: A question entered Sama Pyo’s eyes. I let out a breath as hot as a ball of fire.

hunks.baseline: He shouldn’t have been allowed to leave this world so comfortably, in a single instant.
hunks.sol: He shouldn’t have left this world so easily, in a single instant.

hunks.baseline: Like the Second Elder, whose collarbone had been torn away first, then one arm had been severed, and finally his Eight Extraordinary Meridians had been ripped to shreds before his head was cut off.
hunks.sol: The Second Elder hadn’t. First his collarbone had been torn away, then one arm severed. Only after his Eight Extraordinary Meridians had been ripped to shreds did his head come off.

hunks.baseline: But the grim, hardened expressions on Sama Pyo and Jeok Cheongang—and the First Elder, frozen as if face-to-face with a fiend—gave me some idea.
hunks.sol: But Sama Pyo’s and Jeok Cheongang’s grim, hardened expressions—and the First Elder, frozen as if he’d come face-to-face with a fiend—gave me some idea.

hunks.baseline: His body and voice trembled.
hunks.sol: His body trembled. So did his voice.

hunks.baseline: In the eyes of the old fiend who’d lost his two sworn brothers, the companions of his entire life, in the blink of an eye, I saw rage he couldn’t hide—and fear, even deeper and darker.
hunks.sol: In the eyes of the old fiend who had lost the two sworn brothers he’d spent his life with in the blink of an eye, I saw rage he couldn’t hide. And fear, deeper and darker still.

hunks.baseline: Maybe it was because the blood had soaked the ground. The sound of my footfall rang unusually loud, and the First Elder jumped and stumbled backward.
hunks.sol: Maybe it was the blood soaking the ground, but my footfall sounded unusually loud. The First Elder flinched and stumbled backward.

hunks.baseline: No—he dragged his rear backward, using both arms to brace himself.
hunks.sol: No. He dragged himself back on his rear, bracing himself with both arms.

hunks.baseline: With both knees already shattered, it was the only way he could get even a little farther from me.
hunks.sol: With both knees shattered, it was the only way he could put even a little distance between us.

hunks.baseline: With a scream, the First Elder flung out his arms.
hunks.sol: The First Elder flung out his arms with a scream.

hunks.baseline: I turned my head before I even heard the rush of air. The manifested palm force exploded through the space where my head had been a moment earlier.
hunks.sol: I turned my head before I even heard the rush of air. The manifested palm force blasted through the space where my head had been a moment earlier.

hunks.baseline: Though he was already half-crippled, the powerful internal energy flowing deep within his body still burned like an inextinguishable flame.
hunks.sol: He was already half-crippled, but the powerful internal energy flowing deep within him still burned like an inextinguishable flame.

hunks.baseline: To my eyes, his movements were clumsy beyond words, hopelessly slow—and, because of that, full of openings.
hunks.sol: To my eyes, his movements were clumsy beyond words and hopelessly slow. Every move was full of openings.

hunks.baseline: It was impossible to tell whether his cry was a scream or a battle shout.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t tell whether it was a scream or a battle shout.

hunks.baseline: The First Elder, panicking out of his mind, unleashed palm force after palm force, making the compressed air burst.
hunks.sol: Panicked, the First Elder unleashed palm force after palm force, bursting the compressed air around me.

hunks.baseline: The force of his frenzied attacks whipped my hair around and tore at my skin along with my collar.
hunks.sol: The force of his attacks whipped my hair about and tore through my collar and skin.

hunks.baseline: And that was the First Elder’s final struggle.
hunks.sol: And that was his final struggle.

hunks.baseline: This wasn’t a grappling technique steeped in complex principles, or even a move powered by internal energy.
hunks.sol: It wasn’t a grappling technique built on complex principles, or even a move powered by internal energy.

hunks.baseline: That power and speed, far beyond the limits of a human being, made short work of frail flesh and bone.
hunks.sol: That power and speed, far beyond human limits, crushed frail flesh and bone with ease.

hunks.baseline: His face contorted with pain. A groan forced its way out.
hunks.sol: His face twisted with terrible pain. A stifled groan escaped him.

hunks.baseline: If the old fiend in front of me were the sort to give up everything at a pain like this, the title of the Three Elders of Tianshan would have been forgotten long ago.
hunks.sol: If the old fiend before me were the sort to give up after this much, the name Three Elders of Tianshan would have been forgotten long ago.

hunks.baseline: Five fingers, curled like hooks, flashed down and struck the ground.
hunks.sol: Five fingers curled like hooks flashed down and struck the ground.

hunks.baseline: Just one step.
hunks.sol: One step.

hunks.baseline: I read his movement and stepped back before he could act. His hand narrowly grazed my collar before plunging deep into the earth. I stomped on its back.
hunks.sol: I read his movement and stepped back ahead of him. His hand barely grazed my collar before plunging deep into the earth. I stomped on the back of it.

hunks.baseline: The sensation of his bones shattering traveled up through my sole, the full weight of a thousand catties behind it.
hunks.sol: I felt the bones shatter beneath my sole, a thousand catties of weight behind it.

hunks.baseline: His eyes, wide with unimaginable pain and terror, reflected my calm expression.
hunks.sol: My calm face was reflected in his eyes, wide with pain and terror beyond anything he’d imagined.

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: A precise blow to the jaw turned his head. Yellow teeth flew in every direction with the blood.
hunks.sol: I struck him squarely in the jaw. His head snapped to the side, and yellow teeth flew in every direction with the blood.

hunks.baseline: “When you look at me…”
hunks.sol: “When you look at me like that…”

hunks.baseline: “Like that…”
hunks.sol: “Right now…”

hunks.baseline: “I feel like killing you right now.”
hunks.sol: “It makes me want to kill you.”

hunks.baseline: Gripping the hair of the First Elder, who no longer moved at all, I slowly straightened up.
hunks.sol: I grabbed the First Elder by the hair. He no longer moved at all. Slowly, I straightened up.

hunks.baseline: I was speaking to the monster watching this whole scene from more than thirty yards away, his face alight with excitement—the one who’d cut a thousand people’s heads off with a single gesture.
hunks.sol: I was speaking to the monster watching from more than ten jang away, his face flushed—the one who had cut off a thousand heads with a single gesture.

hunks.baseline: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord gazed at me with admiration, applauding slowly.
hunks.sol: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord applauded slowly, gazing at me with admiration.

hunks.baseline: At his answer, it felt as though the blood in my body were turning cold.
hunks.sol: His answer made my blood run cold.

hunks.baseline: Even now, with extreme rage ruling my mind, the man’s reaction was far beyond anything I could have expected.
hunks.sol: Even with rage consuming me, I hadn’t expected anything like that reaction from him.

hunks.baseline: “That’s how a Murim warrior should be. You have to crush your opponent, cruelly and completely. That’s what makes a real fight, don’t you think?”
hunks.sol: “That’s how a Murim warrior ought to fight. Crush your opponent cruelly and completely. That’s a real fight, don’t you think?”

hunks.baseline: Despite two of the Three Elders of Tianshan—important fighters and his own right hands—being dead, and the third crippled, he looked far happier than he had a moment ago.
hunks.sol: Two of the Three Elders of Tianshan—valuable fighters who served as his own hands and feet—were dead, and the third was crippled. Yet he looked far happier than he had a moment ago.

hunks.baseline: “Isn’t that right?”
hunks.sol: “Well, isn’t it true?”

hunks.baseline: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord blinked at me, then spun around with his arms spread wide.
hunks.sol: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord blinked at me, then spread his arms and turned in a slow circle.

hunks.baseline: “Look at me. My clothes are a bit drab, but compared to you, don’t I look positively mild-mannered?”
hunks.sol: “Look at me. My clothes are terribly drab, but compared to you, don’t I look positively mild-mannered?”

hunks.baseline: “Ah, don’t misunderstand. I’m certainly not saying you look unpleasant. If anything, I find this rather familiar… It’s a good sight, in more ways than one.”
hunks.sol: “Ah, don’t misunderstand. I’m certainly not saying you’re ugly to look at. Quite the opposite. It’s a rather familiar sight to me… Pleasing in all sorts of ways.”

hunks.baseline: At the Blood-Sword Demon Lord’s satisfied smile, I suddenly felt short of breath.
hunks.sol: At his satisfied smile, I suddenly felt short of breath.

hunks.baseline: He’d called it familiar. He’d called it a good sight.
hunks.sol: Familiar, he’d said. Pleasing.

hunks.baseline: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord, of all people. The old, vicious fiend.
hunks.sol: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord, of all people. That old, vicious fiend.

hunks.baseline: Me, drenched in blood from head to toe.
hunks.sol: He was talking about me, drenched in blood from head to toe.

hunks.baseline: Me, a moment ago, consumed not just by revenge but by the desire to inflict even greater pain.
hunks.sol: About the person I’d been a moment ago, consumed not merely by revenge but by the desire to inflict even greater pain.

hunks.baseline: “This… This is, I mean…”
hunks.sol: “This… What I mean is…”

hunks.baseline: A voice I knew all too well cut me off, settled low in a way it rarely was.
hunks.sol: A voice I knew all too well cut me off. It was lower than usual.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang strode forward. I suddenly wanted to ask him something.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang strode forward, and I suddenly wanted to ask him something.

hunks.baseline: But I didn’t ask. No—it was more accurate to say I couldn’t.
hunks.sol: But I didn’t ask. No—I couldn’t.

hunks.baseline: For a moment, I was afraid to ask whether I’d looked like a fiend mad with blood and revenge.
hunks.sol: For a moment, I was too afraid to ask whether I’d looked like a fiend mad with blood and revenge.

hunks.baseline: And yet, somehow, the one who helped me pull my stiffened body and mind back together was that very fiend.
hunks.sol: And yet, ironically, it was that very fiend who helped me steady my stiffened body and mind.

hunks.baseline: “To interrupt us at a time like this, Senior—you’re too cruel. We were having a rather meaningful conversation.”
hunks.sol: “To interrupt us at a time like this, Senior. That’s cruel of you. We were having quite a meaningful conversation.”

hunks.baseline: “Fuck off. This old man never had a junior like you.”
hunks.sol: “Fuck off. This old man has never had a junior like you.”

hunks.baseline: “I know that, but I’ve admired you for a long time, so I can’t help myself. I’ll have to settle for an unrequited love.”
hunks.sol: “I know. But I’ve admired you for so long that I can’t help myself. I’ll have to settle for loving you from afar.”

hunks.baseline: “Do I have to turn you into charcoal while you’re still alive to shut that mouth of yours?”
hunks.sol: “Will you shut that mouth only after I burn you to charcoal alive?”

hunks.baseline: “Probably. To be honest, I was a little disappointed about that. I thought at least one of those three would end up like that.”
hunks.sol: “Probably. To be honest, I was a little disappointed about that. I thought at least one of those three would end up that way.”

hunks.baseline: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord gave a showy sigh, then continued.
hunks.sol: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord gave a theatrical sigh.

hunks.baseline: “You can’t imagine how excited I was when I heard what happened at Mount Jiuhua all those years ago. A descendant of the Fire Gate Clan I’d only ever heard about! When I heard those fools who dared lay a hand on you had all been reduced to ash, I was so delighted.”
hunks.sol: “You have no idea how excited I was when I heard what happened at Mount Jiuhua all those years ago. A descendant of the Fire Gate Clan I’d only ever heard about! And when I heard those fools who dared lay a hand on you had all been reduced to ash—how satisfying that was.”

hunks.baseline: “Isn’t that right? They burned alive—how much pain they must have felt. What could be a surer, more terrible revenge than that?”
hunks.sol: “Well, isn’t it? Burned alive—imagine the pain they must have felt. What revenge could be more certain or more terrible?”

hunks.baseline: “Everyone else shuddered and called you a mad old man, but I didn’t. That was the day I started admiring you.”
hunks.sol: “Everyone else shuddered and called you a mad old man. Not me. I’ve admired you ever since.”

hunks.baseline: At the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, his eyes shining like morning stars, Jeok Cheongang, I, and even Sama Pyo—all of us had been watching the situation calmly—seemed at a loss for words.
hunks.sol: His eyes shone like the morning star. Jeok Cheongang and I were speechless. Even Sama Pyo, who had been watching everything calmly, seemed at a loss for words.

hunks.baseline: More than anyone I’d ever seen, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord was a lunatic worthy of the word.
hunks.sol: More than anyone I’d ever met, the Blood-Sword Demon Lord deserved the word. He was a madman.

hunks.baseline: Now I understood better than ever why the character for “blood” was in his title.
hunks.sol: Now I understood better than ever why “blood” was part of his title.

hunks.baseline: And to the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, the Three Elders of Tianshan were nothing more than livestock he’d kept nearby.
hunks.sol: And to him, the Three Elders of Tianshan were no more than livestock he’d kept close at hand.

hunks.baseline: “Those idiots were the same. During the Great Faction War, they couldn’t run away fast enough whenever the battle turned against them. Then today, they stepped up without knowing their place, so they deserved to die… Ah, come to think of it, one of them’s still alive.”
hunks.sol: “Those idiots, too. During the Great Faction War, the moment a battle started going against them, they couldn’t run fast enough. Today they stepped forward without knowing their place, so they deserved to die… Ah, come to think of it, one’s still alive.”

hunks.baseline: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord glanced at the First Elder, who was still breathing faintly, then turned to me.
hunks.sol: The Blood-Sword Demon Lord glanced at the First Elder, who was still drawing shallow breaths, then looked at me.

hunks.baseline: “I ask only out of concern, but are you thinking of letting him live?”
hunks.sol: “I only ask out of concern, but you aren’t thinking of letting him live, are you?”

hunks.baseline: “He’s been bothering me for a while now. He’s neither alive nor dead… Wouldn’t it be best to make things definite?”
hunks.sol: “He’s been bothering me for a while. Neither alive nor dead… Better to settle it one way or the other, don’t you think?”

hunks.baseline: “If you’re going to kill him, do it quickly. If you want him as a prisoner, have the young fellow beside you take him back. Though he doesn’t know much, so he won’t be of much use.”
hunks.sol: “If you’re going to kill him, do it quickly. If you want a prisoner, have that young fellow beside you take him back. He doesn’t know much, though, so he won’t be much use.”

hunks.baseline: “Ah, though I suppose there’s not much time for that now.”
hunks.sol: “Ah, though perhaps there isn’t time for that anymore.”

hunks.baseline: The war drums were drawing closer, growing louder and more resonant with each beat.
hunks.sol: The war drums were drawing closer, each beat louder and deeper than the last.

hunks.baseline: Behind each of us, the force of countless troops made the air tremble in every direction.
hunks.sol: Behind each side, the aura of countless troops made the air tremble.

hunks.baseline: I could feel it.
hunks.sol: I knew it.

hunks.baseline: The blood-soaked battle for the Great Snow Mountain, the inescapable great war, had finally taken its first step.
hunks.sol: The bloody battle for the Great Snow Mountain—the great battle we could no longer avoid—had finally begun.

hunks.baseline: I couldn’t tell exactly how powerful the Blood-Sword Demon Lord was, but Jeok Cheongang and I should be enough.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t tell exactly how strong the Blood-Sword Demon Lord was, but Jeok Cheongang and I should be enough.

hunks.baseline: Now that the Three Elders of Tianshan, a core part of their fighting strength, were gone, the balance of this battle had tipped heavily in our favor.
hunks.sol: Now that the Three Elders of Tianshan, a core part of the enemy’s strength, were gone, the balance of this battle had tipped heavily in our favor.

hunks.baseline: Surely that was how it would go.
hunks.sol: Surely it had.

hunks.baseline: Why had he treated such important fighters—three Supreme Peak masters—as if they were livestock?
hunks.sol: Why had he treated three Supreme Peak masters—fighters that valuable—like livestock?

hunks.baseline: The moment my thoughts reached that point, my eyes widened.
hunks.sol: The moment that thought came to me, my eyes widened.

hunks.baseline: Dark clouds had gathered at some point. A cold fiercer than the Great Snow Mountain’s own swept toward us, freezing the wind as it came.
hunks.sol: Dark clouds had gathered without my noticing. A cold fiercer than the Great Snow Mountain’s own approached, freezing the wind as it came.

hunks.baseline: And at the center of it all was a company of riders, rushing in like a dark, misty fog.
hunks.sol: And at the center of it all, a company of riders swept toward us like dark mist.

hunks.baseline: As I watched them surge forward with ghostlike movements, not a single thunder of hooves, I remembered.
The otherworldly beings who shouldn’t have appeared here, in the Murim.
hunks.sol: Not even a pounding of hooves accompanied their ghostlike charge. Watching them, I thought of the otherworldly beings who should never have appeared here, in Murim.

hunks.baseline: “Death Knights…?”
hunks.sol: “A Death Knight…?”
